parts.title: My first carnival
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When my family moved to Marlowe Bay last year, I had never been to a carnival. My new classmates talked about it for weeks, and I pretended that I knew what it was. At home I looked it up online, but the photos only made me more nervous. Then a girl in my class asked me to walk in the parade with her group. She said that everybody would be dressed as sea creatures. I said yes before I could change my mind.

We spent three weekends making costumes in her garage. Mine was an octopus with eight long arms made from old tights and newspaper. At first it looked terrible, but after a lot of paint it began to look quite good. On the day of the carnival we met at the harbour at five o'clock. I felt silly in my costume, until I saw hundreds of other people dressed as fish, pirates and even a giant crab.

Then the music began and we started to walk. People on both sides of the street cheered and took photos. My costume was harder to wear than I had expected, because the arms kept catching on the other costumes. Two hours later I was hot, tired and very happy. I had learned that having fun matters much more than looking perfect, and I am already thinking about next year's costume.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer agree to take part in the parade?
options: She had seen photos she liked.
She wanted to wear a costume.
Her family told her to go.
questions.explanation: A girl in her class asked her to walk with her group, and she said yes.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel when she arrived at the harbour?
questions.explanation: She says she felt silly in her costume.

questions.prompt: What changed her feelings at the harbour?
questions.explanation: She felt silly until she saw hundreds of other people dressed in costumes of all kinds.

questions.prompt: What problem did she have during the parade?
options: She could not see the road.
She could not hear the music.
She lost her group in the crowd.
questions.explanation: The arms of her octopus costume kept catching on the other costumes.

questions.prompt: What did the writer learn from the day?
options: Octopus costumes are easy to make.
questions.explanation: She says that having fun matters much more than looking perfect.

parts.title: A village harvest festival
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Every October, a village a few miles from Marlowe Bay holds a harvest festival that is more than six hundred years old. People bring the best vegetables, fruit and flowers from their gardens to the church hall. [1] Last year, a farmer won the prize for the heaviest pumpkin, which weighed more than forty kilos.

On Friday evening, the children walk through the village carrying lanterns they have made themselves. [2] At the top of the hill, hot chocolate is waiting for them.

Saturday is the busiest day. [3] The recipe is a secret, and it has passed from one family to another for generations.

On Saturday afternoon, the whole village joins a long picnic on the green. [4] After the meal, there is dancing until late.

The festival ends on Sunday with a church service of thanks. [5] "It is not about winning," says one of the organisers. "It is about saying thank you."
sentences: Judges then choose the biggest, the tastiest and the most beautiful.
Everyone brings a dish to share, so there is always more than enough.
Everything that is left over is shared with people who live alone.
They sing old songs as they walk, and the villagers listen from their doorsteps.
Last year, the weather was too wet for the lanterns.
Parking is difficult in the village at that time.
Some visitors arrive early to find a good place to park.
Everybody wants to buy the village's spiced apple bread.

gaps.explanation: "Judges then choose" follows the vegetables, fruit and flowers brought to the hall and leads to the prize for the heaviest pumpkin.
"They" are the children with lanterns; they sing as they walk, and "At the top of the hill" continues the walk.
"The spiced apple bread" is introduced before "The recipe is a secret", which refers back to it.
"Everyone brings a dish to share" describes the picnic, and "After the meal" refers to it.
Leftover food shared with people who live alone fits the end of the festival and the organiser's comment about saying thank you.

parts.title: Traditional clothes
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: In many countries, people wear traditional clothes on festival days. These outfits are often [1] by hand, and some take months to finish. A young dancer from Marlowe Bay told me that her costume was [2] to her by her grandmother as a birthday present. The blue pattern on the skirt shows the waves in the bay, and the white shirt is a [3] of respect for the sea. Wearing the clothes is not always [4]: the heavy skirt gets very hot in summer. "However," she says, "[5] I put it on, I feel part of a long story." She hopes her own daughter will [6] the same costume one day.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: Clothes are made by hand, not built; "kept" and "put" do not fit "by hand" either.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: A birthday present is "given" to someone; a costume is not taken, shown or told as a present.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: A "sign of respect" is the common phrase for something that shows respect.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: The heavy skirt gets hot, so wearing the clothes is not always comfortable.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: "Whenever" means every time she puts it on, which fits the feeling she describes.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: You wear a costume; you do not bring, carry or hold it in this sense.

parts.title: A postcard from the festival
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Dear Eitan,
Greetings from Marlowe Bay! We arrived [1] Friday and the festival has already started. The streets are full [2] people in colourful costumes, and there is music everywhere. Yesterday we took part [3] a dance in the street, and in the evening I tried some local dishes for the first time. I wish you [4] here, because you would love the fireworks! We are staying until Sunday, [5] I will tell you all about it [6] I get back.
Sive

gaps.explanation: We use "on" with days of the week: arrived on Friday.
"Full of" is the fixed expression: the streets are full of people.
The phrase is "take part in" something.
After "I wish" about a present situation we use "were": I wish you were here.
"And" adds the next piece of information: they are staying until Sunday and she will tell him everything.
The time clause "when I get back" says when she will tell him.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: erin
turns.text: Karim, have you seen the route of the parade? It starts at the town hall, doesn’t it?

turns.speaker: karim
turns.text: Yes, but this year it finishes somewhere different. Last year it ended there as well, and the streets were completely blocked.

turns.speaker: erin
turns.text: So where do they stop now? At the bus station? That would be easy for people who come by coach.

turns.speaker: karim
turns.text: They thought about it, but the buses need that road all afternoon. In the end they chose a spot by the old lighthouse, at the end of the harbour. There’s more space for the band and the dancers.

turns.speaker: erin
turns.text: Brilliant. I’ll meet you at the harbour then.

question.explanation: The parade used to end at the town hall and the bus station was rejected because the buses need the road, so it finishes at the end of the harbour by the lighthouse.

turns.speaker: petra
turns.text: Hello. I’d like to hire a costume for the festival parade, please.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Of course. We have lots. Have you thought about a clown? Those were very popular last year.

turns.speaker: petra
turns.text: I wore one then, so I want something new. I nearly chose the cat, because it’s so soft and warm, but then I saw the hat with the feather over there.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Ah, the pirate one, with the big black boots and the sword. That’s a lot of fun, and the hat comes with it.

turns.speaker: petra
turns.text: Perfect. I’ll take it for the weekend, please.

question.explanation: She wore the clown last year and nearly chose the cat, but then she saw the hat with the feather, the boots and the sword that belong to the pirate.

turns.speaker: gillian
turns.text: Hi, I’d like a ticket for the Saturday concert, please. Is it sixteen pounds?

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: That’s the price at the door. But if you book online or at this desk before Friday, we take three pounds off.

turns.speaker: gillian
turns.text: Oh, that’s good news. My nephew is eight. Does he need a ticket too?

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Children under twelve get in for ten pounds, but only with an adult. Is he coming with you?

turns.speaker: gillian
turns.text: No, he’s going with his mum. So just one for me, please.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Then that’s your total. Cash or card?

turns.speaker: gillian
turns.text: Card, please.

question.prompt: How much will the woman pay?
question.explanation: The full price is sixteen pounds with three pounds off for early booking; ten pounds is the child price for the nephew, who is not coming with her.

turns.speaker: eszter
turns.text: Good morning, this is the weekend weather report for Marlowe Bay. Yesterday I said Saturday would be sunny all day long, and on Thursday I said cloudy from start to finish, but the new maps show a change. The morning will start with some sunshine, so the early events on the green should be fine. Don’t expect the sun to stay all day, though, because thick clouds arrive around noon, and it will be rainy by the afternoon, with the first drops at about three o’clock. If you’re going to the concert in the evening, take an umbrella. On Sunday the sky will be much brighter.

question.prompt: What will the weather be like on Saturday?
question.explanation: She corrects the earlier forecast: sunshine only in the morning and then clouds at noon, with the first rain at about three o’clock.

turns.speaker: paloma
turns.text: Ladies and gentlemen, this is an announcement from the festival team. The fireworks were going to start at quarter past ten, but the wind is getting stronger and the police have asked us to start earlier. So please note the new time: the first rockets will go up at quarter to ten. The band will carry on playing until half past ten, so you can still listen to the music after the show. Please stay behind the yellow ropes and keep children and dogs close to you. Thank you for your help, and enjoy the evening.

question.explanation: The old time was quarter past ten and the band plays until half past ten, but the fireworks now start at quarter to ten because of the wind.

turns.speaker: maddison
turns.text: Hello, this is a message for the Harbour Gift Shop. I bought a scarf from you yesterday, the blue one with the small boats. I’m calling because I’d like to ask a favour. Your assistant suggested a gift card, but I’d rather give her something to open. I did think of buying a second scarf in green, but one is enough. Please put the first one in paper with a ribbon before Friday. I’ll come and collect it after work. Thanks very much.

question.explanation: She rejects the gift card and the second scarf, and asks the shop to put paper and a ribbon on the one she bought.

turns.speaker: gita
turns.text: Murat, we need volunteers for the family day. I thought you could sell the tickets at the gate.

turns.speaker: murat
turns.text: Sorry, I did that last year and I spent the whole day counting change. And I can’t sing in the choir either. I lost my voice in the spring and it’s still weak.

turns.speaker: gita
turns.text: What about the children’s corner? We have paints, but nobody to help.

turns.speaker: murat
turns.text: Oh, that sounds fun. I’m quite good at drawing, and I like working with kids. Cats, flowers, butterflies on their cheeks.

turns.speaker: gita
turns.text: Perfect. I’ll put your name on the list.

question.prompt: What will the man do at the festival?
question.explanation: He did the tickets last year and his voice is weak for the choir, but he likes the idea of drawing cats and butterflies on children’s cheeks.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: chelsea
turns.text: Sanjay, are you enjoying the concert? You look a bit strange.

turns.speaker: sanjay
turns.text: It’s great, really. The singer is brilliant. I’m standing on the top step, so I can see everything, and I know most of the songs from the radio.

turns.speaker: chelsea
turns.text: So what’s wrong?

turns.speaker: sanjay
turns.text: The music is so loud! The speakers are right behind us and my ears hurt. I can hardly hear you speak.

turns.speaker: chelsea
turns.text: Let’s move to the back, then. We can still hear the band from there.

turns.speaker: sanjay
turns.text: Good idea. I’ll also buy some earplugs from the stall.

question.prompt: What is the problem for the man?
options: He does not know the songs.
question.explanation: Sanjay can see and knows the songs, but the speakers are right behind them and his ears hurt, so the music is too loud.

turns.speaker: yvonne
turns.text: Cormac, my cousins say that the lantern walk is old-fashioned. They’d rather watch a film at home.

turns.speaker: cormac
turns.text: I know some people feel like that. Honestly, I found it a bit slow when I was a child.

turns.speaker: yvonne
turns.text: Me too, at first. But now I love it. My grandmother made the lanterns by hand, and we carry them the same way she did. It’s worth keeping, because if we stopped it, the town would lose something special.

turns.speaker: cormac
turns.text: That’s true. We don’t need to make it modern.

turns.speaker: yvonne
turns.text: Exactly. Some things are better when they stay as they are.

question.prompt: What does the woman think about old traditions?
options: They need to change every year.
question.explanation: Yvonne found it slow as a child, but now she thinks the town would lose something special, and that some things are better when they stay as they are.

turns.speaker: jasmine
turns.text: Have you got any plans for New Year’s Eve, Vijay?

turns.speaker: vijay
turns.text: Not yet. Last year we watched the fireworks in town, but it was freezing and we couldn’t see a thing.

turns.speaker: jasmine
turns.text: I remember. I’d rather not do that again. And staying at home makes the night feel like any other.

turns.speaker: vijay
turns.text: Right. Everybody I know is having a party at Dan’s flat. There’s music and he’s cooking for twenty people.

turns.speaker: jasmine
turns.text: That sounds fun. Shall we take some drinks?

turns.speaker: vijay
turns.text: Sure. I’ll buy the juice if you bring a cake.

question.prompt: What do Jasmine and Vijay agree about New Year's Eve?
options: A party with friends is the best plan.
The town fireworks are too crowded.
A quiet night at home is better.
question.explanation: Both say the fireworks last year were not enjoyable and staying home is boring, so they agree to go to the party at Dan’s flat.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Mauricio, are your lanterns ready for the walk on Friday?

turns.speaker: mauricio
turns.text: Not quite. I haven’t got enough paper, and it’ll take me ages to finish them on my own.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: I thought of buying some in town, but they cost a fortune. And the weather may be bad on Friday, but the other classes are going anyway, so we can’t change the date.

turns.speaker: mauricio
turns.text: So what can we do?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Ask my pupils to help. If everyone brings an old jar and some paper tomorrow, they can make their own in class. They’ll enjoy it more.

turns.speaker: mauricio
turns.text: Good plan. I’ll bring the glue.

question.prompt: What will the teacher do about the lantern walk?
options: Move the walk to another day
question.explanation: Buying lanterns is too expensive and the date cannot change because other classes are going, so she will let the children make their own in class.

turns.speaker: woman
turns.text: The square will be packed on Saturday. Where shall we stand for the parade?

turns.speaker: man
turns.text: By the stage is the usual place, but you have to arrive two hours before to get a good spot.

turns.speaker: woman
turns.text: Too early for me. What about the bridge? It’s a bit of a walk from here.

turns.speaker: man
turns.text: I like it, because you look down on the whole street and the marching bands, from the first drum to the last float. There aren’t any seats, but we can bring a blanket.

turns.speaker: woman
turns.text: Fine. We’ll go to the bridge then.

turns.speaker: man
turns.text: Let’s meet at ten o’clock.

question.prompt: Why do they choose the bridge to watch the parade?
options: They will see the whole parade.
It is near the car park.
question.explanation: The stage needs an early arrival and the bridge has no seats, but from there they look down on the entire street, from the first drum to the last float.

turns.speaker: tourist
turns.text: Excuse me, I’m looking for a souvenir from Marlowe Bay. I like this mug, but it would never survive the flight home.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Fair enough. What about postcards? They’re only fifty pence each, and they weigh nothing.

turns.speaker: tourist
turns.text: They’re cheaper, I agree, but everybody sends postcards. Oh, what are those little ones, with the painted tassels?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Bookmarks. They cost two pounds. A local artist draws the boats and the lighthouse on each one by hand.

turns.speaker: tourist
turns.text: Lovely. I’ll take the one with the harbour.

question.prompt: Why does the tourist choose bookmarks?
question.explanation: The mug is too fragile and postcards are cheaper but ordinary, while the bookmarks are drawn by a local artist with pictures of boats and the lighthouse.

parts.title: A talk about a festival programme
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Good morning, everybody. I’m Easton, one of the organisers of the Marlowe Bay Festival, and I’d like to tell you about the programme. The festival starts on Thursday and finishes on Sunday, so we have four days of events. Last year it was only three, and people asked for more, so we added an extra day. Let me begin with Friday evening. The lantern walk is the most beautiful event of the festival. Children carry paper lanterns through the old streets. It doesn’t begin at the harbour, as many visitors think. We meet outside the library at seven, and the walk takes about forty minutes. On Saturday morning we have a workshop on the green, where a teacher shows you traditional steps. A painting workshop was planned too, but we didn’t find enough space, so only the dance one is running. You don’t need any experience, just comfortable shoes. Then at two o’clock the big parade begins. It starts at the town hall, goes along the seafront and ends by the lighthouse at the end of the harbour. There’ll be bands, dancers and a lot of colourful floats. Please wear something bright if you want to join in. On Sunday we have the craft fair. People often ask if it’s in the church hall, but this year it’s in the old boathouse, which is bigger and has better light. You can buy jewellery, pots, paintings and local honey, and it’s open from ten until five. Finally, tickets. The concert on Saturday night is the only event where you have to pay. You can’t buy the tickets at the door, because we sold out last year. Please go to the tourist office on Harbour Street. They are open every day, and the staff will also give you a free map. Thank you very much for listening, and I hope you enjoy the festival.

gaps.prompt: The event runs for ___ days in total
gaps.explanation: He says the festival starts on Thursday and finishes on Sunday, four days; last year it was three.

gaps.prompt: On Friday evening, people gather outside the ___ for the lantern walk
gaps.explanation: The walk does not begin at the harbour; they meet outside the library at seven.

gaps.prompt: On Saturday morning, a teacher shows traditional steps at a ___ workshop
gaps.explanation: A painting workshop was planned but only the dance one is running.

gaps.prompt: The route of the parade finishes next to the ___
gaps.explanation: The parade starts at the town hall and ends by the lighthouse.

gaps.prompt: On Sunday, the fair of local products is held in the ___
gaps.explanation: It is not in the church hall but in the old boathouse, which is bigger.

gaps.prompt: To buy concert tickets you should go to the ___
gaps.explanation: Tickets are not sold at the door; you go to the tourist office on Harbour Street.

parts.title: An interview with a folk dancer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Ciaran, you have danced in this group for ten years. Why did you go to your first practice?

turns.speaker: ciaran
turns.text: It’s a funny story. I’d seen a show on the main stage when I was six and it was good, but I forgot about it quickly. And a school friend did try to bring me along, though I said no. The one who finally took me was my grandmother. She danced herself when she was young, and she said it would be good for me to see how it works. I haven’t missed a week since.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: So is there anything difficult about it?

turns.speaker: ciaran
turns.text: People think it’s all about memory, but I learned the steps very quickly because we repeat them so often. And I manage to find time to practise, since I do it with the group. What really bothers me are the shoes. They’re heavy, with wooden soles, and after an hour my feet hurt so much that I can’t feel my toes.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: When is the group at its busiest?

turns.speaker: ciaran
turns.text: Winter is quiet, because it’s cold and dark, and we practise only once a week. Weekends and holidays are good, but they’re not the peak either. The craziest time is the town festival in summer, when we perform four times in three days. We get hundreds of requests from restaurants and hotels, and we have to say no to some.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Many groups can’t find young members. How have you managed?

turns.speaker: ciaran
turns.text: We tried to change the dances, but the older dancers hated it, so we gave up. We also asked the school to give free lessons, but the head teacher said there wasn’t time. Then my cousin filmed us and put the videos on the internet. A thousand people watched in a week, and twenty teenagers came to the next practice.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What does the dancing mean to you?

turns.speaker: ciaran
turns.text: It’s good exercise, I suppose, but I could run if I only wanted that. And I’ve been to several countries with the group, though that’s not the reason I stay. The real reason is my family: my grandmother and my father danced these same steps. When I move to the music, I feel that they are standing next to me.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Finally, should the dances ever change?

turns.speaker: ciaran
turns.text: Some people say never, but I disagree, because a living tradition has to grow. I don’t want to make them very modern either, with electronic music, for example. What I like is a small change, like a new tune or a different order. It keeps the spirit and keeps the dancers interested.

questions.prompt: Why did Ciaran first go to a dance practice?
options: He had seen a show and liked it.
questions.explanation: His grandmother took him; he had seen a show but forgot it, and the school friend failed to bring him.

questions.prompt: What does Ciaran find difficult?
questions.explanation: He learned the steps quickly and finds time to practise; what bothers him are the heavy shoes.

questions.prompt: When is the group busiest?
questions.explanation: Winter is quiet and weekends are not the peak, but the town festival in summer is the craziest time.

questions.prompt: How has the group attracted young people?
options: By giving free lessons at school
questions.explanation: Changing the dances failed and the school had no time for lessons, but the videos on the internet brought twenty teenagers.

questions.prompt: What does the dancing mean to Ciaran?
options: A good way to stay fit
questions.explanation: Exercise and travel are not the reason he stays; his grandmother and father danced the same steps, so it links him to his family.

questions.prompt: What does Ciaran think about changing the dances?
options: A few small changes are good.
They need to be much more modern.
questions.explanation: He says never is wrong and very modern is not what he wants; small changes keep the spirit and the dancers interested.
